content: The American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers, commonly referred to as ASHRAE and pronounced as ash-ray, is an international technical organization that serves individuals and organizations with an interest in heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration (HVAC&R). ASHRAE is structured into Regions, Chapters, and Student Branches, which facilitate the exchange of knowledge and experiences in the HVAC&R field for the benefit of both professionals and the general public. The organization provides numerous opportunities for members to contribute to the development of new knowledge, particularly through research and participation in its Technical Committees. These committees convene twice annually during the ASHRAE Annual and Winter Meetings. Additionally, the AHR Expo, a prominent product exhibition, is held in conjunction with the Winter Meeting. ASHRAE publishes the ASHRAE Handbook, a comprehensive four-volume resource on HVAC&R technology. The volumes are titled Fundamentals, HVAC Applications, HVAC Systems and Equipment, and Refrigeration. ASHRAE also produces a widely recognized series of standards and guidelines that address various aspects of HVAC systems and related issues. These standards are frequently cited in building codes. Examples of ASHRAE Standards include: Standard 34: Designation and Safety Classification of Refrigerants Standard 55: Thermal Environmental Conditions for Human Occupancy Standard 62.1: Ventilation for Acceptable Indoor Air Quality (earlier versions were referred to as 62 prior to 2004) Standard 62.2: Ventilation and Acceptable Indoor Air Quality in Low-Rise Residential Buildings Standard 90.1: Energy Standard for Buildings Except Low-Rise Residential Buildings Standard 135: BACnet A Data Communication Protocol for Building Automation and Control Networks These standards are periodically reviewed, revised, and republished, making the year of publication critical for compliance with building codes. ASHRAE also publishes the ASHRAE Journal, a monthly magazine that features peer-reviewed articles on the practical application of HVAC&R technology, updates on upcoming meetings and product exhibitions, classified and display advertisements, and editorials. Members of ASHRAE receive the ASHRAE Journal and the current year's volume of the ASHRAE Handbook as part of their membership benefits. In addition to these resources, ASHRAE publishes books, ASHRAE Transactions, and the International Journal of HVAC&R Research. ASHRAE was established in 1894 during a meeting of engineers in New York City. Initially known as the American Society of Heating and Ventilating Engineers (ASHVE), the organization changed its name in 1954 to the American Society of Heating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHAE). In 1959, ASHAE merged with the American Society of Refrigerating Engineers (ASRE) to form the current ASHRAE. Despite its name, which includes American, ASHRAE is a globally influential organization with 55,000 members worldwide who are committed to advancing the arts and sciences of HVAC&R. The organization's headquarters is located in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.
